analysis.title: UBS Warns Hedge Funds Are Capitulating As Goldman Says "Our Phones Are Exploding"
key_insights: UBS high-touch flows opened roughly 2:1 better for sale on Nov 5, 2026. Hedge funds were 23/75/2 buy/sell/short sell, with the sharpest selling in Tech, particularly Memory and Semis.

Long-only flow was net buy at 55/45, but the VIX spike alongside the sell skew pointed to meaningful risk reduction. UBS saw the clearest capitulation in its Neoclouds and Semis baskets, which it describes as a delayed reaction to the prior day's election results.
Retail supply was showing up in Tech. UBS flagged the timing of the SOXX stock split against the move. The selloff over the prior 30 minutes appeared futures-driven.
Hyperscalers were giving back part of Nov 4's gains, adding pressure to the broader indexes.

UBS Risk Control rebalance estimates: $95-105bn of selling on a 2% SPX decline and $50-55bn of buying on a 2% rally. A +/-1% move implies about $15bn of selling, and a +/-50bp move implies $10-15bn of buying.

Goldman's equities desk (John Flood) said Nov 4 was one of its busiest days of the year by trade count and notional, and Nov 5 was the opposite. Long-only clients were frozen, and hedge funds were selling hyperscalers they bought the day before. Flood saw no buyers stepping in to defend anything yet.
Flood described the pressure as top-down, applied through macro instruments. Volumes vs 20-day averages: SPY +160%, QQQ +100%, SMH +150%, DRAM +75%.

Goldman's semis argument: by 2028 there may not be enough data center shells (land, power, shell) for the semiconductors being built, so there would be too many chips. Pressure is also acute in engineering and construction stocks, independent power producers (especially Texas, Georgia and Ohio exposure) and Neoclouds.

Permitting-driven bottlenecks in land, power and shell make traders cautious on memory names (HDD, DRAM, NAND) that benefited from higher ASPs and supply/demand imbalances. Multiples are contracting as investors worry 2028 gigawatts added could be about flat y/y with 2027, versus the more than 30% y/y growth in GW or capex that investors had anticipated.

Goldman Prime Brokerage (Marco Laicini): on Nov 4 broader markets rose but a semis-to-software rotation drove a sharp US momentum sell-off. Systematic L/S ended slightly up on EM Asia gains, global fundamental funds rose, and multi-strategy funds were modestly lower.

Goldman Prime Brokerage on Nov 5 around 10:30 EST: US markets sold off and global momentum fell. Fundamental funds were down, with US-focused funds hit harder, and TMT was severely down. Systematic funds were positive and multi-strategy funds were down significantly on equity exposure.

sector_views.rationale: Goldman's desk cites a view that 2028 data center shell capacity (land, power, shell) will fall short, leaving too many semiconductors. Selling was heaviest in semis.
Traders are cautious on memory names that gained from higher ASPs and supply/demand imbalances, as 2028 data center growth may be closer to flat than the expected 30%+.

sector_views.sector: Data center construction and power (E&C, IPPs)
sector_views.rationale: Acute pressure reported in E&C stocks and IPPs, especially those with Texas, Georgia and Ohio exposure, on permitting bottleneck concerns.

risk_factors: Data center shell bottleneck from land, power and permitting constraints could cap 2028 GW additions and leave excess semiconductor supply.
Memory pricing (ASPs) could reverse if data center buildout growth slows from the expected 30%+ y/y.
No buyers stepping in to defend the selloff, with long-only investors frozen.
Futures-driven, macro-instrument selling pressure could continue.
Retail supply in Tech and the SOXX stock split timing add to selling pressure.
vol_and_positioning: UBS: VIX spiked alongside a sell skew in hedge fund flows (23/75/2 buy/sell/short sell), pointing to meaningful risk reduction.
UBS: capitulation signs are clearest in Neoclouds and Semis baskets, with retail supply also appearing in Tech.

UBS Risk Control rebalance: $95-105bn of selling on a 2% SPX decline, $50-55bn of buying on a 2% rally, about $15bn of selling on a 1% move either way, and $10-15bn of buying on a 50bp move either way.
Goldman desk: long-only community frozen, no buyers defending, retail-heavy brokers report a second day of notable sell skews.
Goldman desk volumes vs 20-day average: SPY +160%, QQQ +100%, SMH +150%, DRAM +75%.

Goldman Prime Brokerage: TMT severely down on Nov 5, US-focused fundamental funds hit harder, systematic funds positive, multi-strategy funds down significantly. On Nov 4 a semis-to-software rotation drove a sharp US momentum sell-off.
geopolitical: US midterm election results of Nov 4, 2026 are cited as the trigger for a delayed reaction in hedge fund selling, after heavy de-risking into the midterms.

tension_points.bull_case: Investors had anticipated more than 30% y/y growth in GW or capex in 2028 at the top of the cycle, supporting semis and memory pricing.
tension_points.bear_case: Land, power and shell permitting bottlenecks could leave 2028 GWs added closer to flat y/y with 2027, producing too many semiconductors for too few data center shells.
tension_points.what_invalidates: 2028 GWs added coming in closer to flat y/y with 2027 rather than above 30% y/y growth.
